Ruling recorded: the lane is parked correct-and-inert, default off, and parking
is safe because refuseGlobalTagsOnEagerPath means a converted page can only fail

Revival needs BOTH, and either alone leaves the lever not worth shipping: every
read path that can touch a converted page must be lazy (today lazyEligible =
pointLookup && trxIntentLog == null, so scans, serializer walks and column fills
are eager), and the +16.6 % chunked-body framing must decompose to something
small.

Also records the method error, because it is the transferable part: "requires
lazy chunks" went into this document, into two error messages and into a memory,
and passed two reviews and a five-arm gate without anyone asking when the system
actually reads lazily. A premise written as a REQUIREMENT reads as an
instruction to the future; written as a DEPENDENCY on a named mechanism it shows
the gap on first read. Write the condition, not the requirement.

[improvement](build) Fully exclude OBS/COS deps via --exclude-{obs,cos}-dependencies (#66564)

## What

Turn the existing `--exclude-obs-dependencies` and
`--exclude-cos-dependencies` build flags into a **full exclusion** of
the respective cloud provider (Huawei OBS / Tencent COS): when passed,
nothing from that provider is resolved, compiled, or bundled into the FE
binary.

## Why

The two flags were introduced in #58071 as a `scope=provided` downgrade.
That only kept the jars out of the shipped artifact — Maven **still
resolved and downloaded** them at build time. In particular
`com.huaweicloud:hadoop-huaweicloud:3.1.1-hw-46` is published **only**
on Huawei's own Maven repo (`repo.huaweicloud.com`). Environments that
cannot or must not reach it (corporate proxies blocking the host, or
compliance constraints forbidding Huawei/Tencent artifacts) still could
not build the FE, because resolution was unconditional. The flags now do
what their names imply.

## How

Active-by-default Maven profiles `obs` / `cos`, deactivated via
`-Ddisable.obs=true` / `-Ddisable.cos=true`, wrap every touch point:

- **fe-core**: the `fe-filesystem-obs` / `fe-filesystem-cos` test
couplings.
- **hadoop-deps**: the `hadoop-huaweicloud` dependency and the Huawei
OBS Maven repository.
- **fe-filesystem**: the `fe-filesystem-obs` / `fe-filesystem-cos`
modules (which transitively pull the Huawei / Tencent SDKs).

`build.sh` maps `--exclude-obs-dependencies` → `-Ddisable.obs=true` and
`--exclude-cos-dependencies` → `-Ddisable.cos=true` (replacing the old
`*.dependency.scope=provided` mapping), and drops the corresponding
provider from **both** the `-pl` reactor list **and** the filesystem
plugin packaging loop, so the reactor and the dist layout stay
consistent when a provider is excluded.

## Behaviour

- **Default builds are unchanged** — the profiles are active unless a
flag is passed.
- `sh build.sh --fe --exclude-obs-dependencies` builds the FE with no
Huawei artifact resolved and no OBS code compiled or bundled; same for
`--exclude-cos-dependencies` and Tencent COS.

## Testing

- `mvn help:active-profiles` on `fe-core`, `fe-filesystem`, and
`hadoop-deps`: `obs`/`cos` active by default, and absent with
`-Ddisable.obs=true` / `-Ddisable.cos=true`.
- Confirmed fe-core has no compile-time import of the OBS/COS provider
classes (loaded via SPI/reflection), so `compile` and `test-compile`
stay green when the profiles are off.
- `xmllint` on all changed poms and `bash -n build.sh` pass.

refactor(screens): thin artist, album and search screens

The artist screen orchestrated providers in render — calling provider hooks,
merging local and external results, deciding enrichment — across 614 lines of
Content and 478 of Header, refetching albums in both. The album screen split
into LocalAlbumBody and ExternalAlbumBody: two component types for one album
that differ only in what the player can do with its tracks. Search was 819
lines with provider-specific legs dispatched by name.

Each is now a screen model and a screen. Route params resolve to one entity,
one resolved detail, and a set of decisions computed once — discography
classification, similar-artist dedup, counts, playability — leaving the
components to render decisions rather than make them.

An album's tracks carry a typed playability instead of the album carrying a
type: full, preview with its clip, or unavailable. That is the distinction
that was real; two component identities was not.

Phase 5 closes here. `resolveArtistInfo`, `resolveArtwork`,
`useArtistInfoEnrichment`, `useArtworkEnrichment` and `enrichmentFetchers` are
deleted, along with `useExternalArtist`, `useExternalAlbum`, `LocalAlbumBody`
and `ExternalAlbumBody`. Enrichment now runs through one attributed path, and
the plan's rule that a phase is not complete while both implementations remain
callable is satisfied rather than deferred.

Search kept the thing worth protecting. `planSearchLegs` — the sole authority
on Library XOR Other Sources — is unchanged byte for byte, and its nine
assertions are unmodified, so the decomposition moved code around the state
machine without touching it. SearchContext went from thirteen provider-name
references to none.

Provider names are finally leaving feature code. The broker built in Phase 3
now has callers, and names live only where a provider declares itself.

  provider refs  151 -> 140
  file-shape      15 -> 13
  unused exports 600 -> 587
  coverage     66.1 -> 69.38%
  tests         1598 -> 1614

Two things worth recording rather than burying. Porting the artwork-enrichment
test caught a real bug in the new Header before it landed: the first draft
preferred a resolved cover whenever one existed, instead of falling back to it
only when the artist had none of its own — which would have let an integration
override server artwork, the exact rule the test exists to protect. And a test
deleted in the belief that it only covered a removed hook was restored on
inspection: it also covered three hooks that survive.

One deviation is deliberate and unfinished: external search routes through
`SourceDefinition.search` on the sources registry rather than the capability
broker, because `CapabilityMap` declares no search-by-text capability yet.
That is the next thing to close, not a resting place.

Speed up hashing, probing, and erase

Three independent optimizations, ~2.4% geomean improvement on
bench_quick_overall_udm (verified with interleaved A/B runs):

- wyhash: process 96 bytes per iteration with 6 independent lanes
  (extra secret constants from rapidhash), halving the serial
  multiply-chain depth for keys > 96 bytes. ~8% faster for 200 byte
  strings, ~20% for 1000 bytes.

- next(): use a bitwise AND with the (power of two) bucket mask
  instead of a compare-and-wrap branch against bucket_count(). The
  shift loops cache the mask in a local so uint32 stores into the
  bucket array can't alias it.

- do_erase(): prefetch the erased and the last value before the
  shift-down loop; both are needed right after it. ~4% faster
  random insert/erase for uint64_t keys.

fix(standalone): wait out stale OPFS handles instead of going in-memory

A page reload (the settings "restart" button, a service-worker update, F5)
starts a new database worker while the browser is still releasing the
previous worker's exclusive OPFS sync access handles. An immediate
installOpfsSAHPoolVfs() in that window fails with NoModificationAllowedError
and reacts by deleting the pool directory, which only the very handles that
caused the failure keep from succeeding. The boot then fell back to an empty
in-memory database ("data will not persist"), which to the user looks like
every note vanished; TRILIUM_INTEGRATION_TEST builds threw "SAHPool is
required for integration tests" instead, which is the recurring "User can
change language from settings" timeout on the linux-arm64 standalone e2e
job. Nothing there is ARM-specific — those runners are just slow enough to
lose the race: on an idle 4-core x64 it never fired, while under CPU
contention 3 of 6 runs lost it.

The worker now waits for every pool file to accept a probe access handle
before installing the VFS (waitForSahPoolRelease, 15s budget), and installs
it exactly once. Waiting first keeps the acquisition failure, and with it
the pool-deleting cleanup, from happening at all; a retry loop would run
that cleanup once per attempt and can resurrect an empty pool over the
user's data. The wait runs before the log service opens its own OPFS file,
which the same teardown holds, so post-reload sessions keep file logging.

An installSahPool() failure past that point is a broken environment, not a
transient: it now ends the boot through the existing fatal path
(WORKER_ERROR -> error-overlay.ts) with a message naming OPFS, instead of
silently opening a database whose contents are an illusion.

Under the contention that reproduced the CI failure, the language-change
test passes 8 of 8 repeats, every run's trace showing the race firing and
being waited out, and no NoModificationAllowedError reaching sqlite-wasm.

feat(agent): the chart agent, a right-rail panel in /trading

The agent now sits beside the chart, sees what is on it, and draws on it.
Analyse the chart, find candlestick and chart patterns, draw levels, a
trendline or a channel, shade a demand or supply zone, and clear what it drew.

Most of the plumbing already existed and had never been connected: the chart
surface and its prompt section, the ChartCommand wire type, _runtime_lines to
render context into the prompt, and getChartContext and onChartCommand on the
stream hook. Nothing emitted or sent any of it.

Two safety properties carry this feature.

Everything the agent draws is namespaced ai:{group}:{index}, assigned in one
place so the prefix cannot be applied on one path and forgotten on another,
and the agent has no tool that can name or remove a drawing the operator made
by hand. An agent that wipes an operator's markup is worse than one that draws
nothing.

fix: [notifications] stop shared-session detachment and prepared-statement desync

Production showed two failure families in the notification daemon.

First, "Instance is not bound to a Session" storms: every gathered
process_notification task shares one scoped session, and each task's
finally block closed it — detaching the Notification instances all the
other in-flight tasks were still holding, so the first task to finish
stranded the rest of the batch. The per-task close is removed; the
fetch loop already releases the session once per cycle after the whole
gather completes. The factory also sets expire_on_commit=False so one
task's commit no longer forces redundant re-SELECTs in every other.

Second, both directions of psycopg3 prepared-statement desync
("_pg3_N already exists" and "does not exist") — the signature of
connection-pooling middleware in transaction mode swapping the server
session between transactions. Named prepared statements are disabled
engine-wide (connect_args prepare_threshold=None, merged into the
instance's engine options); parameters are still bound server-side, so
the cost is negligible.

internal: url, Leave the user out of a userless SCP-like endpoint ParseSCP builds an ssh:// URL from the three components of an SCP-like endpoint, and it always set User, even when there was no user to set. net/url draws a distinction there that this erased: url.User("") is an empty userinfo, not the absence of one. An endpoint of `github.com:user/repo.git` came back as `ssh://@github.com/user/repo.git` — a URL naming no user that does not parse back to itself — and every `URL.User != nil` check downstream read it as a user having been given.

The SCP-like form spells the user as an optional `[<user>@]` prefix, so
its absence is part of the answer. The user is now only attached when
one was written.

What changes for a caller: transport.ParseURL and the internal parser
return a *url.URL whose User is nil for an endpoint written without a
user, where it was previously a non-nil empty userinfo, and String()
renders `ssh://host/path` instead of `ssh://@host/path`. The ssh
transport already fell back to its default username for an empty one, so
no connection is made differently; code that tested `URL.User != nil` to
decide whether a user was supplied now gets the answer it was asking
for.

##### Features

[#​22494](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22494)

- \[cli] Implement the `filesystem__grep` and
`filesystem__content_replace` local tools
for `pulumi neo`. `grep` runs a regex search across files in the project
root
with an optional `include` glob filter and returns results in
`path:lineno: line`
form. `content_replace` performs a literal multi-file search-and-replace
with a
`file_pattern` glob and `dry_run` preview mode. Both tools skip binary
files,
hidden directories, and `node_modules`, and reject paths outside the
project
    root. Their input schemas match the cloud-side tool definitions.

[#​22655](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22655)

- \[cli] Add `pulumi_preview` and `pulumi_up` as local tools for the
experimental `pulumi neo`
agent. The Neo TUI renders a persistent bordered block for each
operation that
streams changed resources and diagnostics as the engine runs and
finalizes with a
    summary of the op counts. Hidden behind PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL.

[#​22697](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22697)

[#​22693](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22693)

##### Bug Fixes

- \[engine] Return a clear error when two installed plugins claim the
same default provider package name (for example, a native `scaleway`
provider alongside a `terraform-provider` bridge parameterized as
`scaleway`) instead of panicking with "Should not have seen an older
plugin if sorting is correct!"
[#​22679](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22679)

- \[programgen] Do not wrap a `call(...)` on a method whose return type
is marked plain in an Output. Previously
PCL bound every method call's return type as `Output<T>`, which caused
downstream program-gen
to emit broken `.apply(...)`/`.ApplyT(...)` traversals against plain
struct returns (e.g.
methods with `liftSingleValueMethodReturns=true` or
`ReturnTypePlain=true`).

[#​22696](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22696)

- \[backend/diy] When using a backend url containing creds (e.g.
PostgreSQL conn string), mask user:pass as in lock-related error
messages
[#​22701](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22701)

- \[codegen/go] Generate unqualified `Provider` references for the
package's own provider resource. Previously
the Go codegen always emitted `<pkg>.Provider` even when the reference
appeared inside `<pkg>`
itself, producing identifiers that would not compile. Affects generated
code for method return
types (and other schema positions) that reference
`pulumi:providers:<pkg>`.

[#​22696](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22696)

- \[codegen/nodejs] Generate unqualified `Provider` references for the
package's own provider resource when emitting
TypeScript code inside that package. Previously the generator always
qualified the name as
`<pkg>.Provider`, which does not resolve when no `<pkg>` namespace
import is in scope.

[#​22696](https://redirect.github.com/pulumi/pulumi/pull/22696)

- \[codegen/nodejs] Import the correct class name for a provider
resource. Imports for `pulumi:providers:<pkg>` used
the title-cased package name instead of `Provider`, producing a phantom

HTTP-FLV: Preserve forwarded client IP behind a reverse proxy. v8.0.14 (#4711)

## Summary

Preserve the original HTTP-FLV viewer address supplied by a reverse
proxy instead of replacing it with the proxy's TCP peer address.

## Problem

SRS already parses `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-IP`, but
`SrsLiveStream::serve_http_impl()` unconditionally replaced the parsed
address with `hc->remote_ip()`. As a result, HTTP-FLV client statistics
and the SRS console displayed the reverse proxy address rather than the
viewer address.

## Changes

- Prefer the original address from `X-Forwarded-For` or `X-Real-IP` for
HTTP-FLV viewers.
- Fall back to the TCP peer address when neither header is present.
- Add regression test
`ReproduceIssue4621.PreserveForwardedIpForHttpFlvClient`.

Pin that a dimmed empty-day placeholder stays out of the motion cohort

past_event_opacity now reaches empty-day notices, so a placeholder can carry
past-event alongside empty-day-title for the first time. The obvious worry on
reading that change is that a newly classified row starts scrolling, and nothing
pinned the answer: the existing placeholder cases add and remove empty-day-title
to set up unrelated cohort scenarios rather than asserting the guard itself.

Three cases, each with its own control, because "did not animate" is otherwise
evidence about the harness rather than about the guard. A marked placeholder is
retired to pending with no animation while an identically overflowing sibling
keeps running; it cannot lead a cohort even as the only overflowing title; and —
the load-bearing one — dropping empty-day-title while KEEPING past-event lets it
rejoin at the next boundary. Without that third case the first two would pass
equally well against a guard that wrongly suppressed every finished event's
title, which is the opposite defect and just as easy to ship.

Removing the controller's empty-day-title test fails 6 of the file's 20 cases
against a 20-passing control, so these detect the guard rather than restating it.

fix: validate PAC CLI path to prevent mutable variable hijack (#6414246) (#1386)

Adds security validation to BuildToolsRunnerParams.runnersDir to ensure
the PAC CLI path read from POWERPLATFORMTOOLS_PACCLIPATH points to the
official PowerPlatformToolInstaller task directory.

A low-trust build step could previously overwrite the mutable job-scoped
variable to redirect protected tasks to an attacker-controlled PAC binary,
allowing credential theft via the service-connection auth flow.

The fix validates that:
1. The path is under the agent's _tasks directory
2. The path contains a known ToolInstaller task GUID (LIVE/BETA/DEV/EXPERIMENTAL)

If either check fails, the task fails closed before materializing any
service-connection credentials.

fix(snippets): discard stale session on workspace-edit apply (#5639)

When a code action with a SnippetTextEdit is applied through
workspace.applyEdit, insertBufferSnippets used to call cancel(true) on
the buffer's snippet session. That only paused synchronization and kept
the previous snippet object alive, including a 'current' placeholder
that an intervening undo may have already orphaned. The next apply then
took the nested-expansion branch in start() and grafted the new snippet
onto the stale tree, producing corrupted output (existing arm body
re-indented and the new arm appearing twice in the rust-analyzer 'Fill
match arms' reproduction from #5448).

Calling deactivate() instead clears the snippet/current state so start()
always takes the clean branch for workspace-edit driven insertions.

Fixes #5448

[FlyDSL] gfx942 fp8_mqa_logits: let _auto_variant choose rows_per_block (#4963)

* [FlyDSL] gfx942 fp8_mqa_logits: let _auto_variant choose rows_per_block

_auto_variant returned f"mfma_r2_w{wpb}", so rows_per_block was pinned at 2 and
seven of the nine registered variants -- including every member of the r4 family
-- could never be selected.

r4 amortizes each KV tile load over twice as many query rows and is faster from
seq_len 8 upward. The gap is widest exactly where it costs most: vLLM chunks
indexer prefill to fit VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB (512 MB), which caps
seq_len at 1024 when seq_len_kv is 131072, so the existing seq_len >= 2048 branch
cannot fire at long context and every such call took mfma_r2_w4 -- the median of
the nine by speed, with the best 1.65x faster.

Measured on MI325X (gfx942), seq_len_kv 131072, best variant vs the r2 pick:

  seq_len    1   r2 25.2 us    r4 79.1 us     r4 3.1x worse
  seq_len    4   r2 24.3 us    r4 31.5 us     r4 1.3x worse
  seq_len    8   r2 34.0 us    r4 32.9 us     r4 1.03x better
  seq_len   16   r2 56.5 us    r4 47.5 us     r4 1.19x better
  seq_len 1024   r2 2564.3 us  r4 1520.3 us   r4 1.69x better

Below seq_len 8 the host padding of seq_len up to a multiple of RPB dominates --
at seq_len 1 an r4 kernel computes 4 rows to obtain 1 -- so r2 is kept there and
behaviour for those shapes is unchanged.

Logits are bitwise identical across all variants at every shape tested, so this
is purely a blocking/occupancy change.

End to end on 8x MI325X, TP8, GLM-5.2-FP8, 131072 in / 1024 out, concurrency 8:
median TPOT improves 7.22% and output throughput 6.60%. This kernel is 16.8% of
GPU time at that point.

Signed-off-by: Jin Tao <jin.tao@amd.com>

* [FlyDSL] gfx942 fp8_mqa_logits: pick RPB on element count, and keep it a divisor

Refines the previous commit's rule after a 2-D sweep. That rule keyed RPB off
seq_len alone with a crossover measured only at seq_len_kv=131072; sweeping the
other contexts shows the crossover is not a seq_len threshold at all, and that a
second effect was being read as one.

RPB tracks the logits element count. Over seq_len 1..8192 x seq_len_kv
1024..262144 on MI325X, the boundaries land on the same element count at every
context: RPB=1 wins below 2**19 elements (27/27 shapes), RPB=2 at 2**19 (6/6),
RPB=4 from 2**21 up (38/38), with 2**20 a transition band split 3/3. Keying off
seq_len instead put the previous rule on the wrong side at low context: at
seq_len 16, seq_len_kv 1024 it chose RPB=4 and ran 1.26x slower than RPB=1.

RPB must also divide seq_len. When it does not, the launcher pads with four
torch.cat calls; that is a flat ~44 us of host-side overhead, independent of
seq_len_kv, and it is the whole of the "small seq_len" penalty the previous
commit attributed to wasted rows. At seq_len 1, seq_len_kv 131072: RPB=1 23.1 us,
RPB=2 67.8 us, of which the four cats are 44.1 us and pre-padding by hand
recovers all of it (21.9 us). So the penalty is not proportional to the padding
-- 1 wasted row of 2 costs the same as 3 of 4 -- and it applies to every odd
seq_len, which the old rule sent to RPB=2 unconditionally.

Stepping down to a divisor is only right while the kernel is cheap relative to
that fixed cost, so it is gated to the same 2**21 elements: at seq_len 1025,
seq_len_kv 131072 the dividing RPB=1 takes 3880 us against 2601 us for a padded
RPB=2.

Measured on MI325X, no FLYDSL_FP8_MQA_LOGITS_VARIANT set, old pick vs new:

  seq_len  seq_len_kv        old         new   speedup
     1024      131072   r2_w4 2598.7   r4_w4 1623.5    1.60x
     1025      131072   r2_w4 2609.3   r4_w4 1594.0    1.64x
      512      131072   r2_w4 1190.1   r4_w4  795.3    1.50x
      700       50000   r2_w4  661.6   r4_w4  440.3    1.50x
      333       12000   r2_w4  118.4   r4_w4   97.1    1.22x
       16      131072   r2_w4   58.3   r4_w4   47.4    1.23x
        3      131072   r2_w4   66.4   r1_w4   28.1    2.36x
        1      131072   r2_w4   69.4   r1_w4   23.2    2.99x
        1        1024   r2_w4   66.2   r1_w4   22.2    2.98x

No shape measured regresses; the smallest gain is 1.04x. Against the best of the
nine variants at each shape, pooled over held-out data (non-power-of-two shapes,
a fine seq_len sweep, and head counts 16 and 64), the geometric mean cost falls
from 1.45x to 1.03x and the worst case from 3.17x to 1.41x.

Logits are bitwise identical across all nine variants at all 180 shapes swept
(1620 timings), so this remains purely a blocking/occupancy change.

WPB is deliberately left alone. It is worth a few percent at most here, and
unlike RPB its optimum moves with the head count -- at 64 heads the current
WPB rule costs 1.61x worst case where a fixed WPB=4 costs 1.07x -- so it needs
its own sweep rather than a change fitted to one head count.

MQE: Split and cache instant queries for functions over range operators (#13472)

#### What this PR does

Introduce an MQE optimisation to split and cache results of functions
over range vectors, to make repeated evaluation of queries over long
ranges more efficient (e.g. for rule evaluation). This is the initial
implementation that is experimental and only supports for instant
queries.

Splitting is controlled by a feature flag and a configurable split
interval (defaulting to 2h) and disabled by default. An optimization
pass identifies splittable range vector function calls and rewrites them
into a `FunctionOverRangeVectorSplit` operator that divides the query
range into a head, cacheable aligned blocks, and a tail.

The `sum_over_time`, `count_over_time`, `min/max_over_time`, `rate`,
`increase` functions are supported for splitting. The splitting is done
in a generic way, with each function defining its own protobuf
intermediate representation and serialization.

Ranges within the out-of-order time window are not cached to avoid
returning stale results.

Annotations are supported, with relevant annotations being stored as
part of cache entries if needed. There is one known unsupported case for
annotations where sum_over_time may not emit counter reset warnings when
the conflicting hints span split boundaries (more details in the code
comments).

**For reviewers**

recommended order to review them in:

Identifying appropriate nodes that can be split and deciding how to
split the range vector
-
`pkg/streamingpromql/optimize/plan/rangevectorsplitting/optimization_pass.go`
- `pkg/streamingpromql/optimize/plan/rangevectorsplitting/node.go`

Executing the splitting and caching
- `pkg/streamingpromql/operators/functions/split_operator.go`

Cache
-
`pkg/streamingpromql/optimize/plan/rangevectorsplitting/cache/cache.go`

Split function implementations
- `pkg/streamingpromql/operators/functions/split_model.go`
- `pkg/streamingpromql/operators/functions/split_functions.go`
- `pkg/streamingpromql/operators/functions/split_rate_functions.go`

Main bulk of tests
- `pkg/streamingpromql/range_vector_splitting_test.go`
-
`pkg/streamingpromql/testdata/ours-only/range_vector_splitting_2h.test`
- Note that `split_operator_test.go` also runs all the promql tests in
`TestQuerySplitting_UpstreamTestCases` and
`TestQuerySplitting_OurTestCases` with different split intervals to get
more test coverage

Rough implementation for splitting and caching partial parts of instant
queries for functions over range vectors. Currently only works for
`sum_over_time()` (though it doesn't do Kahan summation properly) and
does not work for subqueries.

Initially I tried getting something working for both range and instant
queries. I got something to pass tests ([see these
commits](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/pull/13472/files/0112ea2cb89954a98f66217650a8f43e646b6592)),
but the code got very complex, so I simplified to just instant queries
for now.

This isn't in a state to be merged, the PR is just opened to show the
current progress and allow for initial comments

Overview:
- Added query splitting optimizer
([ref](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/compare/intermediate-cache-new?expand=1#diff-b42f9171a7548d3d745186ec4e475389dbb0af842867cd9e0539bbb970d5dc77))
which goes through the nodes. If it finds a sum_over_time() function
with a range vector selector that can be split with at least one split
being cacheable, it'll create a new SplittableFunctionCall node over the
FunctionCall node.
- Materializing SplittableFunctionCall creates a newly introduced
FunctionOverRangeVectorSplit operator
[ref](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/compare/intermediate-cache-new?expand=1#diff-e95df51ed9ba7269dc05b930411dea095ebefcabb97a9bb620f413d3a457b447).
This should give the same results as FunctionOverRangeVector, but with
the query splitting and caching logic.
- The split operator has a reference to the inner range vector selector
node (instead of inner materialized operator).
- Most computation happens in SeriesMetadata() functions at the moment.
I don't think SeriesMetadata is the best place to do all the work, it
was just the simplest thing to implement for now.
- SeriesMetadata() will load all the cache results to see what gaps
there are. Uncached splits are merged if they're contiguous, and a
RangeVectorSelector operator is materialized for each split. When
calling SeriesMetadata() for each uncached split, loading samples and
calculating the intermediate result is done (this part could be deferred
later).
- The FunctionOverRangeVectorSplit keeps track of a series -> split
mapping. When NextSeries() is called, it just moves to the next series
in the mapping, gets the results for each split and merges them.
- The current code assumes series from the inner operator aren't sorted
lexicographically. For range vector selectors, we can assume sorted I
think, but possibly not with subqueries.
- Storing results back into the cache is done in
FunctionOverRangeVectorSplit.Finalize()
- The splits are calculated based on the _query_ time range at the
moment. To be more effective, they should be calculated based on time
ranges of the blocks loaded from storage (i.e. take into account offset
and @ modifier)
- Query splitting tests
[here](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/compare/intermediate-cache-new?expand=1#diff-f6b64351048b57c4c0debc148c7201df62317b5da289aa5e9269cfce073ce4ac).
They all pass. Also ran Mimir locally in ingest storage mode and logs
show splitting and caching is happening.
- This implementation is not very memory efficient at the moment - all
the intermediate results are held in memory until Finalize() is called
for FunctionOverRangeVectorSplit. This includes the seriesmetadata for
each split.

(Autobahn) Share vote aggregation (CON-423) (#4152)

## Summary
- Fold prepare/commit/timeout vote aggregation into one weighted
aggregator and one phase adapter. The three phases still differ in
bucket key (vote hash vs view), QC constructor, and quorum getter; they
no longer duplicate the latest-vote-per-key / monotonic-QC loop.
- Shared tests cover below-quorum, quorum emit, ignore equal/stale, and
replace-at-newer-view. Each phase keeps a QC-validity test plus the
property that is actually its own: conflicting prepare/commit proposals
do not form a QC; timeout votes with differing prepare-QC payloads still
do. Same-view votes after a QC at a non-genesis view leave the published
QC unchanged.
- Ingest is unchanged: verify outside the lock, then insert. Published
QC behavior matches main (`qc.Load()`, then `New*QC`, then `Store`).

## Quorum wiring
`PrepareQuorum`, `CommitQuorum`, and `TimeoutQuorum` are already the
same function on main (`totalWeight - Faulty()`; prepare/timeout/app
return `CommitQuorum()`). The phase tests size the committee with
`CommitQuorum()` and do not pin which getter is wired into each adapter.

If those thresholds diverged later, swapping the wrong getter would not
always fail this suite (a too-strict aggregator in particular would
still form a QC). We are not adding two-sided per-phase quorum tests for
that: we do not expect the getters to diverge in the near future.
`QC.Verify` would still catch the too-loose direction.

feat(telemetry): correlate Hermes and Claude Code traces across processes

* feat(telemetry): correlate Hermes and Claude Code traces across processes

Both emitters minted their own trace ids, so a Claude Code session launched
by a Hermes turn appeared as an unrelated trace. A shared session id could
group them but never showed that one launched the other.

Both now read a W3C traceparent from the environment and join that trace,
parenting their root span on the supplied span. Hermes publishes its active
tool span through child_env(), or — behind LATITUDE_HERMES_EXPORT_TRACEPARENT
— by scoping the variables onto os.environ around each tool call, so any
subprocess inherits them. LATITUDE_PROJECT rides along because ingest is
project-scoped and a mismatch splits the trace silently.

An inherited trace id is shared by every turn of a session, so the turn
coordinates move into the Claude Code span-id salt; without that, turn 2's
first call reuses turn 1's span id whenever a call has no message id. That
would inflate the additive trace rollups, which have no dedup.

Also fixes headless emission, which the feature depends on: the Stop hook
was registered async, and Claude Code registers an async Stop hook but exits
before spawning it in headless mode, so `claude -p` emitted nothing at all.
The hook is now synchronous and hands its work to a detached worker, which
blocks the turn for 0.06s rather than the 0.77s an inline run costs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(telemetry): address review on cross-harness trace correlation

Span ids on an inherited trace were salted with the reported session id,
which one Hermes run hands to every child it launches. Two children of the
same run share trace id, session id and turn number, so their interaction
spans collided and one replaced the other under ReplacingMergeTree. The
salt now uses Claude's own session id, which is per process.

The reported session id fell back to the local one whenever the trace was
not joined — no valid header, or past the join ceiling — contradicting the
documented contract that a capped session stays grouped by the shared id.
Both harnesses now read LATITUDE_SESSION_ID independently of the header.

Python's `or` skipped an empty LATITUDE_TRACEPARENT and joined the
unrelated TRACEPARENT it was meant to suppress; precedence is now by
presence, matching the Claude Code side. Field validation moved to
fullmatch/whitespace rejection, since `$` also matches before a trailing
newline in both languages.

The opt-in os.environ export overwrote its undo record on every tool call,
so overlapping calls restored each other's values and leaked TRACEPARENT
past the tool call. The export is now owned by one call at a time; a
concurrent one is skipped rather than handed the wrong span.

The stale-payload sweep deleted every old entry in a user-configurable
directory, so pointing it at a shared directory made the Stop hook delete
unrelated files. It now only removes files it wrote.

* fix(claude-code): register SessionEnd so headless runs emit at all

The hook was registered only on Stop with async: true. Claude Code registers
an async Stop hook but exits before spawning it in headless mode, so
`claude -p` emitted nothing — a probe hook never executed once under async,
while the same hook registered synchronously ran and received its payload.
Headless is how one harness drives another, so cross-harness correlation
could not work at all.

Registers a synchronous SessionEnd hook alongside it rather than making Stop
synchronous. Stop stays async, so interactive turns are untouched; going
synchronous there would have cost ~0.32s per turn, since the shipped command
resolves through npx and pinning the version does not avoid it (measured:
0.320s for @latest, 0.317s pinned, 0.032s for a resolved local path).

SessionEnd also fires on interactive quit and on Ctrl-C, catching a final
turn whose async Stop hook died with the process. Only SIGKILL escapes both.
Unknown hook events are ignored by Claude Code, so the entry is inert on
versions predating it. The two never double-count: emission is incremental
behind a byte offset and a state lock.

The fix applies SQL-standard quote escaping (`'` → `''`) in four places within `searchFilters.tsx`: - **`filtersToQuery`**: Escapes `'` as `''` when wrapping string values in SQL single quotes for `IN`/`NOT IN` conditions - **`splitValuesOnComma`**: Recognizes `''` as an escaped quote inside quoted strings, instead of treating it as a string boundary - **`getBooleanOrUnquotedString`**: Unescapes `''` back to `'` when stripping surrounding quotes from parsed values - **`extractInClauses`**: Handles `''` correctly when splitting conditions on `AND` inside quoted strings This fix also applies to dashboard filters since `useDashboardFilters.tsx` imports the same `filtersToQuery`/`parseQuery` functions. ### How to test locally or on Vercel 1. Open the search page and add a sidebar filter whose value contains single quotes (e.g. filter on `message = "my 'filter' key"`) 2. Confirm the filter is applied correctly and the query executes without errors 3. Remove and re-add the filter to confirm round-trip parsing works (filter state is correctly restored from the SQL condition) ### References - Linear Issue: HDX-3902 Linear Issue: [HDX-3902](https://linear.app/clickhouse/issue/HDX-3902/filter-keys-dont-support-quotes)

[Jobs] Run managed-job-status-refresh as a main-process thread (#9731)

* [Jobs] Run managed-job-status-refresh as a main-process thread

The managed-job-status-refresh daemon was scheduled on the shared
executor task queue, which in HA mode lets the daemon drift to a
different replica from the controllers it spawned: a BrokenProcessPool
or worker SIGKILL on the holder pops the daemon onto a sibling replica,
where ha_recovery_for_consolidation_mode runs controller_process_alive
against PIDs that live in another pod's PID namespace, declares them
all dead, and respawns a parallel set of controllers.

Bind the daemon's lifecycle to the API server main process by running
it as a thread (started in the supervisor, not in lifespan — lifespan
runs per uvicorn worker).  The daemon, the consolidation_mode lock it
holds, and the controllers it spawns now share a single process / pod
lifecycle.

The PG advisory lock can still go silently stale while main is alive
(idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, NLB idle, RDS restart, etc.); add
PostgresLock.is_session_alive() so the thread probes the lock's
underlying session every 5s and SIGTERMs itself on loss, letting K8s
restart the pod and the remaining replicas re-elect a leader.

Tests:
- PostgresLock.is_session_alive: not-acquired / no-connection /
  SELECT 1 success / SELECT 1 raises.
- ManagedJobRefreshDaemonThread state machine: dispatches PostgresLock
  vs other DistributedLock for liveness, sends SIGTERM to self on
  lock loss, gates start on consolidation mode.

* Refine

Signed-off-by: Aylei <rayingecho@gmail.com>

* Address gemini-code-assist review

- Touch the rolling-restart signal file only after we hold the lock.
  With the daemon thread starting on every replica, standby replicas
  blocked in acquire() would otherwise leave a stale signal file
  forever and update_managed_jobs_statuses would early-return on them.
- Decouple the lock probe from the event-loop sleep. The inner loop
  used to sleep events.EVENT_CHECKING_INTERVAL_SECONDS (20 s) per
  iteration, so the lock probe fired ~20 s apart instead of the
  intended 5 s. Now the loop ticks at 1 s with separate cadences for
  the probe and the event run.
- In the outer except block, distinguish between "acquire() itself
  failed" (retry) and "we held the lock and the session died"
  (SIGTERM). Otherwise a transient recovery failure plus a lost PG
  session would keep us in the retry loop as a stale leader while
  another replica acquired the lock cleanly.

Tests cover the three new branches.

* Fix pylint and test_daemons after refactor

- Move sky.jobs.constants to top-level imports
- Drop redundant except (SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt) re-raise
- Remove TestConsolidationEventInstancePersistence cases that referenced
  the now-deleted _managed_job_consolidation_mode_lock and managed_job
  event in sky.server.daemons (logic moved to ManagedJobRefreshDaemonThread)

* [Jobs] Restore managed_job_status_refresh_event stubs for pickle compat

After the managed-job-status-refresh daemon was rewritten as an in-process
thread, the pickled InternalRequestDaemon rows from older server versions
in HA deployments reference daemons.managed_job_status_refresh_event and
daemons.should_skip_managed_job_status_refresh via their event_fn /
should_skip attributes. pickle.loads raises AttributeError on every poll
of those rows, generating a flood of internal /api/get 500 responses
during a rolling upgrade.

Restore both symbols as no-op stubs so that pickle.loads succeeds. The
daemon-orphan cleanup path will then delete those orphan rows because no
matching INTERNAL_REQUEST_DAEMONS entry exists for the pickled daemon id.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Kill local job controllers on consolidation lock loss

When the managed-job refresh daemon's PostgreSQL session dies
(idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, NLB idle, pg_terminate_backend,
etc.), the advisory lock is released server-side and another replica
can immediately acquire it. Until now, _suicide_on_lock_loss just
sent SIGTERM to the API server and relied on the up-to-60s drain to
eventually free the controllers via kernel PID-namespace cleanup.
During that window, the new leader's ha_recovery sees ALIVE jobs
with no local controller and spawns fresh ones — splitting writes
with the still-running old controllers.

Tighten the window from "until drain finishes" to ~0:

* Add scheduler.kill_local_job_controllers() that reads the local
  controller PID file, skips dead/stale records via
  controller_process_alive(), and SIGTERMs each live PID. Idempotent
  and best-effort.

* In _suicide_on_lock_loss, re-touch the recovery signal file (so any
  in-flight submit_jobs short-circuits maybe_start_controllers) and
  call kill_local_job_controllers() before sending the API-server
  SIGTERM. Both new steps are best-effort and never block the SIGTERM.

The graceful-shutdown path in uvicorn does NOT need this — while the
session stays alive, the daemon thread holds the lock until the
supervisor exits, and at that instant the kernel SIGKILLs every
process in the pod's PID namespace, so the controllers cannot
outlive the leader transition.

Tests: unit tests for kill_local_job_controllers (live/stale/missing
file/permission errors); _suicide_on_lock_loss touches the file and
kills before SIGTERM, in that order; touch failure does not block
SIGTERM.

* Use pathlib.Path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

Replace the try/except FileNotFoundError around signal_file.unlink()
with the missing_ok=True kwarg, which has been available since
Python 3.8 and is the idiomatic form used elsewhere in the codebase.

* Update sky/jobs/managed_job_refresh_thread.py

Co-authored-by: gemini-code-assist[bot] <176961590+gemini-code-assist[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* [Jobs] Stop refresh thread after _suicide_on_lock_loss

`_become_leader_and_run` returns normally only after the inner loop's
probe detected lock loss and called `_suicide_on_lock_loss` — every
other exit path raises. The outer `run()` loop was catching that
return and immediately re-entering, where:

  - `is_locked()` returns True (stale local `_acquired` flag; only
    `is_session_alive()` knows the server-side lock is gone),
  - the acquire branch is skipped,
  - `ha_recovery_for_consolidation_mode()` runs,
  - and `scheduler.maybe_start_controllers()` is called without
    `from_scheduler=True`, so the recovery signal-file gate at
    scheduler.py:237 is bypassed.

Fresh controllers get spawned via `launch_new_process_tree` (nohup +
setsid) under a now-released lock. Meanwhile, the new leader on the
other replica is doing the same — both replicas run controllers for
the same managed jobs for the duration of the API server drain
(~60s), splitting writes to managed-job state. This is exactly the
failure mode `_suicide_on_lock_loss` was supposed to prevent. The
preceding "Kill local job controllers on consolidation lock loss"
commit made it strictly worse: now the suicide kills all controllers,
so the re-entry sees `alive=0` and faithfully spawns a fresh set
rather than no-op'ing on `alive == wanted`.

Add a `return` after the normal-return path so the thread stops
instead of looping. New test covers the invariant: `run()` calls
`_become_leader_and_run` exactly once when it returns normally.

* [Jobs] Touch recovery signal file before acquiring consolidation lock

Restore the pre-refactor ordering: the recovery signal file must exist
before we block on acquire(), so that during a rolling update no new
controller can be started on this replica before recovery runs. Add a
regression test pinning the touch-before-acquire contract.

* Migrate from Newtonsoft.Json to System.Text.Json and drop net462 target

**Rationale and scope**

Remove Newtonsoft.Json external dependency from the core library and CLI,
replacing it with System.Text.Json (available in .NET Standard 2.0 via NuGet
as of 6.0; we use 9.0.1 for netstandard2.0). Drop net462 target framework
from the library: .NET Framework 4.6.2 extended support ended January 12, 2026,
and is now out of support. NuGet consumers on .NET Framework can use the
netstandard2.0 asset from this package without requiring net462.

**Changes**

- Library targets: retain net10.0, net8.0, netstandard2.0; drop net462
- CLI target: net10.0 only
- Remove Newtonsoft.Json dependency from Certes.csproj; add System.Text.Json
  9.0.1 for netstandard2.0 targets
- Replace JsonConvert.Serialize/Deserialize with JsonSerializer equivalents
- Replace [JsonProperty(name, Order=X)] with [JsonPropertyName(name)] and
  [JsonPropertyOrder(X)] on all ACME resource models
- Update JsonUtil to use JsonSerializerOptions with PropertyNamingPolicy.CamelCase
  and JsonStringEnumConverter
- Replace enum converters: StringEnumConverter → JsonStringEnumConverter
- Update CLI ConsoleExtensions, UserSettings, and AzureDnsCommand to use
  System.Text.Json; configure WriteIndented for formatted output
- Make JWK properties (JsonWebKey, EcJsonWebKey, RsaJsonWebKey) public to enable
  System.Text.Json serialization (Newtonsoft.Json serialized internal properties
  by default; System.Text.Json does not)
- Add Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4 override to CLI and test projects to prevent
  vulnerable 10.0.3 transitive dependency from Azure SDK

**Verification**

- All 192 unit tests pass on net10.0 (enum serialization now uses strings per
  RFC 7519; test expectations and JsonSerializerSettings updated to match)
- Library and CLI packages build successfully in Release configuration
- RFC 7638 JWK lexicographic ordering preserved via [JsonPropertyOrder]
  attributes; test confirms EC and RSA keys serialize with correct property order
- No vulnerable packages in dependency graph after refresh

**Compliance**

This constitutes a library update with no public API surface changes, though
serialization formats differ slightly from Newtonsoft.Json (enums as strings
rather than numbers, consistent with RFC 7519 examples and web standards).
Callers using JSON round-trip scenarios should validate enum handling.

**AI assistance:** Prepared with OpenCode using claude-haiku-4.5.
**Verification:** All unit tests pass (192/192), packages build, no regressions

instead of the RFC-compliant lowercase values from [EnumMember] attributes.

Type-level [JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter))] attributes were

fix(grbl): heal flow-control state jammed by lost acks (issue #428)

After a soft reset, some firmwares (the Sculpfun iCube over Bluetooth
in issue #428) acknowledge the post-cancel safety shutdown commands
with silence; acks can also vanish on a flaky link. Their pending
entries then jam the driver forever: every later 'ok' is
mis-attributed to a stale FIFO entry, and
execute_interactive_command() blocks on an unbounded
pending_queue.join() — 'Read from Device' hangs and the machine
controls appear dead while status polls keep working.

- GrblSerialTransport now timestamps the oldest un-acked command
  (oldest_pending_age()).
- execute_interactive_command() waits via _await_pending_drained(),
  which resets the flow-control state once the oldest pending entry
  outlives STALE_PENDING_ACK_TIMEOUT (10 s) instead of deadlocking.
- The idle connection loop heals such stale state proactively, so
  the queue unjams within seconds even without user interaction.
- Healing never runs while a job is streaming, where un-acked
  entries age legitimately during long moves.

fix(anomaly): use zlib.crc32 for RSHash slot assignment

RSHashCountMinSketch._indices mapped a discretised vector to a slot with
hash((key, payload)). CPython salts hash() for bytes and tuple inputs from
PYTHONHASHSEED, which is randomized per process, so a seeded RSHash produced
different scores in different processes.

Replace the salted hash with zlib.crc32, seeded from the table key. The key
still steers its own table, so the detector seed still reaches slot
assignment, but the result no longer depends on the interpreter's hash salt.

Measured on TinyBlobs, RSHash AUC with seed=42 is 0.781305 before and after,
so the 0.78 pin in tests/test_anomaly_detectors.py does not move. Individual
scores do change (6 of 1100 on TinyBlobs), so this is a behaviour change for
existing users.

Add tests/test_rshash_reproducibility.py, which asserts reproducibility
across processes with different PYTHONHASHSEED values, that the sketch keys
keep the tables independent, and that the detector still consumes its seed.

oidc_child: support Entra onPremisesImmutableId identifiers

Hybrid Active Directory and Entra ID deployments cache the AD objectGUID
as the user UUID, while the Entra ID userinfo response returns a
separate cloud-generated id. The two never match, so authentication
with id_provider = ad and auth_provider = idp always failed.

Add idp_auth_user_identifier_attr so deployments can select which
userinfo or token attribute identifies the authenticated user. When it
is set to onPremisesImmutableId, oidc_child base64-decodes the value
and converts the objectGUID bytes with guid_blob_to_string_buf(),
producing the same UUID string SSSD stores for AD users.

The option has no provider-derived default. More than one attribute can
link an Entra ID object to its on-premises counterpart, depending on how
Entra Connect selects the sourceAnchor, so the attribute has to be named
explicitly. If the configured attribute is missing or cannot be decoded,
authentication fails rather than falling back to another attribute.

Move identifier extraction out of oidc_child_json.c into
oidc_child_user_id.c so it is independently testable, and add cmocka
coverage for the default attributes, a configured plain attribute,
objectGUID decode vectors, and the failure cases.

Document the option in sssd-idp.5, including the objectGUID encoding,
the ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid sourceAnchor caveat, and the Graph $select
requirement.

Resolves: https://github.com/SSSD/sssd/issues/8574

:feature: Active Directory and Entra ID hybrid setups can now use Entra
  ID for authentication while identities come from AD. Setting
  `idp_auth_user_identifier_attr` to `onPremisesImmutableId` makes
  `oidc_child` decode the synchronized AD objectGUID so it matches the
  UUID stored in the SSSD cache.

:config: New option `idp_auth_user_identifier_attr` selects the userinfo
  or token attribute used to identify the authenticated user. It has no
  default and must be set explicitly for AD and Entra ID hybrid
  deployments. The `idp_userinfo_endpoint` has to request the attribute
  with `$select`.

Fix Leaflet element outliving its client through Layer.current_leaflet (#6345)

### Motivation

Fixes #6339.

After the last `ui.leaflet` on a page has been used, the map element
stays reachable for the life of the process: deleting the client removes
it from `client.elements`, but `Layer.current_leaflet`, the `ClassVar`
that `Leaflet.__enter__` and `Leaflet.__getattribute__` write so a new
layer can find its map, still points at it and is cleared nowhere. The
element, its `layers` list and anything those layers close over are kept
alive until the next `ui.leaflet` anywhere in the process replaces them.
With a `ui.label` on the same page, the label is collected after
`client.delete()` and the map is not.

### Implementation

This is option 1 from the issue, the small fix: `Leaflet._handle_delete`
clears `Layer.current_leaflet` when it points at the element being
deleted, before delegating to the parent. Two lines in
`nicegui/elements/leaflet/leaflet.py`; the class variable and the
`__getattribute__` binding stay as they are, so nothing changes about
how a layer finds its map while the map is alive. The proper fix,
passing the map to each layer explicitly and dropping the class
variable, changes how layer classes are reached and is left for 4.0 as
the issue suggests.

`tests/test_leaflet.py` gains
`test_leaflet_is_collected_after_client_deletion`, the issue's `User`
test with a marker added so the layer graph is part of what must be
collected: it opens a page with a `ui.leaflet`, deletes the client, runs
`gc.collect()` and asserts the weak reference to the map is dead.

- base, before this change: `3 passed`
- with only the new test applied to the base tree: `1 failed, 3 passed`,
the failure being the new test with the map still alive
- with this change: `4 passed`

Every result above was produced on Windows 11 with CPython 3.14.3; the
`Screen` test in the same file ran in the same session under the `User`
fixture's plugin. Linux and the rest of the supported matrix were not

PR #45428: [XLA] Fix wrong reshape dimension in while-loop concat code motion

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45428

### Problem
`WhileLoopConcatCodeMotion` crashes with a `CreateReshape` element-count `CHECK` failure on valid HLO when a grouped op has a **shared operand** that must be broadcast and the concatenation is on a **non-zero dimension** whose size differs from dimension 0.

### Root cause
In `RewriteLoopWithConcatGroups`, when a group element's operand is shared across the group it is broadcast and then reshaped to merge the broadcast dimension into the concat dimension:

```cpp
if (!operand_inserted_concat_dim) {
  // Concat on existing dim. Reshape to merge the broadcast dim.
  data_shape.set_dimensions(
      operand_concat_dim,
      data_shape.dimensions(operand_inserted_concat_dim) *   // <-- bug
          group.elements.size());
  broadcast = body->AddInstruction(
      HloInstruction::CreateReshape(data_shape, broadcast));
}
```

`operand_inserted_concat_dim` is a `bool`. Using it as the argument to `dimensions()` reads dimension `0` (since `false == 0`) instead of the concat dimension. The new dimension size is therefore computed from the wrong dimension. When `dimensions(operand_concat_dim) != dimensions(0)`, the reshaped shape has a different element count than the broadcast, and `CreateReshape` fails its `ShapeUtil::ElementsIn` `CHECK`, aborting compilation.

The intended value is the concat dimension's own size, which is exactly the dimension being overwritten by `set_dimensions(operand_concat_dim, ...)`.

### Fix
Read the size of `operand_concat_dim`, not dimension 0:

```cpp
data_shape.set_dimensions(
    operand_concat_dim,
    data_shape.dimensions(operand_concat_dim) * group.elements.size());
```

When the concat is on dimension 0 (the case the existing tests cover) the two indices coincide, so this is a no-op there and only corrects the non-zero-dimension case.

### Test
`SharedBroadcastOperandNonZeroConcatDim`: a while loop whose body concatenates two `f32[3,5]` group elements on dimension 1 and feeds each through an `add` with a shared operand. The shared operand takes the broadcast+reshape path; under the old code the reshape targets `f32[3,6]` (18 elements) from a `f32[3,2,5]` broadcast (30 elements) and crashes. With the fix it reshapes to `f32[3,10]` and partitioning succeeds.

Split morloc.h into .h and .c files

Now rather than importing morloc.h header into the nexus and every
language binder and building independently, we build it once and reuse
the shared library. Previously, a single Morloc build might need to
compile this library twice, once for the nexus file and once for any C++
files (the R and Python binders already used shared libraries).

Claude did most of the work here, which was quite an educational process
for me. Interestingly, the AI cannot easily read a file this size, so to
sort the implementation from the specification (the functions from the
prototypes, type defititions, and macros) it decided to write a Python
function. I suggested it used ctags, which it did. And it seemed to have
worked. However, much to my dismay, I found that it left all the C
function leading comments in the header file. So I will need to manually
munge them back in. Or just delete them, most of them weren't great
comments anyway. Maybe it is best to just go through all the code
carefully and reanalyze it.

Claude it a fantastic job of debugging. The move to a single shared
library exposed some inconsistencies in our ABI. There were two
compilers at work, gcc and g++, which have some differences. In the
process of debugging the errors we were seeing, Claude found that there
were memory alignment issues in the shared memory volume. I knew the
cause of that, I'd specified that the packet structs all have the
"packed" attribute so that the optimizer wouldn't mess with their layout
(which you don't want when you are specifying a binary format). But I
hadn't done the same for the shared memory format. I recommended Claude
add in these attributes, and that solved the memory alignment problem.

But there was a second problem. This one was beautifully simple and
subtle. It would have taken me a long time to catch it. There was a
communication issue between the nexus and the C++ pools (and only the
C++ pools). The pool was returning CALL packets to the nexus. This was
occuring because the pool was identifying every incoming packet as a
ping, even if it wasn't, and returning it unchanged. The reason for this
was due to the definition of a boolean.

The original morloc.h file had the clause:

```
  #ifndef bool
  # define bool unsigned
  #endif
```

This will define a bool as an unsigned integer (4 bytes) if the macro
term "bool" is not already defined. This expression is from the
MessagePack library that was included in the morloc.h header. But the
morloc.h header also included stdbool.h, which had its own defintion of
a bool as a 1 byte character. C++ has a keyword bool, not a macro, so
`#ifndef bool` evaluates false and bool will be given a 4 byte value.

In the original setup, morloc.h was included into every file and the
declarations and definitions were compiled together. The new
implementation separated them. So code generated by the C++ compiler
would use 4 byte bools and code generated by the C compiler would use 1
byte bools. Thus when the pool (generated by the C++ compiler) asked the
shared library (generated by a C compiler) if a packet was a ping
packet, the library would return a 1 byte response. The pool would
interpret it as a 4 byte bool. The remaining 3 bytes would usually be
non-zero, leading to truthy garbage values.

So, overall, apart from the AIs desecration of my comments, it did a
great job.

library, providing a dynamic array with Python-like list operations.

- `append(item)` - Add items with automatic capacity growth (2x
strategy)
- `len(list)` - Get current length
- `list[i]` - Read element by index
- `list[i] = value` - Modify element by index
- Negative indexing support (`list[-1]` for last element)

### Mutations
- `pop()` - Remove and return last element
- `insert(i, item)` - Insert at position with element shifting
- `clear()` - Remove all elements
- `remove(value)` - Remove first occurrence by value

### Iteration
- `__fastiter__()` - Fast iteration protocol
- `for x in list:` - Full for-loop support via `list_iterator` struct

### List operations
- `extend(other)` - Append all elements from another list
- `copy()` - Create shallow copy with independent memory
- `+` operator - Concatenate lists into new list
- `*` operator - Repeat list elements n times

### Searching
- `index(value)` - Find index of first occurrence
- `count(value)` - Count occurrences

### Comparison
- `==` operator - Type-safe equality using `@blue.metafunc`

## Implementation Details

- Uses low-level `ptr[T]` for memory management
- Generic implementation via `@blue.generic`
- Struct-based with `ListData` containing length, capacity, and items
pointer
- `@typelift` decorator for lifted type implementation

ops)

  - Empty lists
  - Single elements
  - Capacity growth beyond initial size
  - Negative indexing boundary conditions
  - Type-specific operations (int, f64)
  - Error cases (IndexError, ValueError)

## Example Usage

```spy
from _list import List

def example() -> str:
    lst = List[int]()
    lst.append(10)
    lst.append(20)
    lst.append(30)
    
    lst[1] = 99          # Modify by index
    lst.remove(10)       # Remove by value
    
    lst2 = lst.copy()    # Shallow copy
    lst3 = lst + lst2    # Concatenate
    
    result = ''

vello_common: Cull line segments outside of the clip during flattening (#1954)

Since #1519, flattening skips Bézier segments that lie fully to the
right of, above, or below the clip's bounding box, but straight line
segments were always emitted. The tiler only culls against the viewport,
so lines outside the clip but inside the viewport still go through
tiling and strip rendering, only to be thrown away by the clip
intersection. This applies the same test to line segments, including the
implicit closing ones, by the same argument as for curves: such a
segment affects neither coverage nor winding inside the box.

The right and bottom edges of the cull box are now rounded out to the
tile grid, as clip boxes already are. Without a clip the cull box is the
viewport, which the tiler culls in whole tiles, so flattening now never
drops a line the tiler would keep.

This matters most for line-heavy content under a small clip, such as
drawing a whole UI clipped to a damage rect. In a local benchmark (strip
generation for a whole synthetic 1280x960 UI scene of 320 cards under
one clip), a 256x128 clip goes from 2.53 ms to 1.18 ms, and the lines
reaching the tiler drop from ~28k to 3.3k. Without a clip, strip
generation is unchanged within noise. Flattening alone is ~4% slower
there on the line-heavy scene, because the new check only repeats the
viewport culling the tiler does anyway.

Tests: a flatten test pinning which lines get culled (strip-row
alignment of the top edge, continuing after a culled `ClosePath`, culled
implicit closes), one pinning that lines in the last partial tile column
and row are kept, and a strip generator test checking that generating
under a clip gives exactly the strips of generating unclipped and then
intersecting with the clip. The tiler regression test for #1126
flattened a path that is now culled entirely, so it builds its lines
directly.

* fix: keep masked points out of the transform in from_unstructured

used.

stays in the mesh, so it takes the position of the first point that
isn't masked. Before, it sat wherever its fill value landed, which
stretched the bounds of the mesh. With every point masked nothing is

connectivity array never applied it, so those points are transformed as

Decode telemetry frames on the host and show them in monitor.py (#356)

### Motivation

Closes #343, part of #340.

The frame format from #342 is decoded once, in the Lizard repo:
`monitor.py` shows frames with field names, and other host software can
use `telemetry.py` instead of reimplementing the format.

As discussed below, the PR also adds a layout ID to the format of #342,
which is not released yet, so that a frame ID that gets new fields is
not decoded with its old layout.

### Implementation

- **Layout ID** (firmware): frames and layout lines carry one more byte,
the low byte of the CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over the frame's fields as
`name:type`, separated by spaces. The header is frame ID, layout ID,
sequence number and millis, 7 bytes instead of 6; the layout line is
`__LAYOUT__v1 1.0/3 bf motor.position:f`. At the 180-byte payload limit
the body grows from 188 to 189 bytes, which is still 252 Base64
characters. Different fields get the same ID with a chance of 1 in 256.
- **`telemetry.py`** uses only the standard library and runs on Python
3.8, like `monitor.py` on a Robot Brain with L4T 35. `Decoder.feed(line,
sender=None)` returns a `Text`, `Layout` or `Frame` and keeps the
layouts per sender. A line `bus[N]: …` counts as peer N's, already now
for #344. `split_checksum` and `checksum` strip and check the `@xx` line
checksum.
- **A frame** is a line starting with `~` that is valid Base64, at least
header plus CRC long and has a matching CRC-16; anything else stays
text. A frame that cannot be decoded gets `no_layout`,
`layout_incomplete`, `layout_mismatch` or `unknown_version` and shows
its payload in hex. Floats are shown with `%.7g`.
- **Layouts**: a frame is decoded only with a complete layout of its
frame ID and layout ID, i.e. all indices up to the `/count` of its
layout lines. A layout line with another layout ID or another count
starts the frame's layout anew, and so does a line that differs from the
stored one under the same ID, i.e. other fields that happen to get the
same ID. Lines that match keep the layout, so frames keep decoding while
`core.telemetry_info()` repeats it. Sequence numbers play no part in

Add a Windows CI leg for the storage file-lock tests (#6160) *Opened by Claude Code on evnchn's behalf.* ### Motivation Our CI matrix is Ubuntu-only, but a whole class of `Storage.clear()` / `FilePersistentDict` teardown bugs is **Windows-only** — `PermissionError [WinError 32]` when a storage file is unlinked while an in-flight backup still holds it open (see #6159, #6158). These are invisible to us today: #6159's regression tests are green on Linux *with or without* the fix, because the race can't occur on POSIX. This adds one narrow, cheap Windows job to close that blind spot. ### Implementation - **New `windows-test` job** in `ci-gate.yml` on `windows-2022`, running `pytest tests/test_storage.py -m "not screen"` — the non-browser storage tests. On current `main` these are exactly the three file-race/teardown tests from #6159, i.e. the tests that only have teeth on Windows. The job takes under a minute. - **New `screen` marker**, registered in `pyproject.toml` and auto-applied by a small `conftest.py` hook to every test that uses the browser-based `screen` fixture — so the Windows job selects by mechanism, not by a hand-maintained test list. - **Gating:** the job is wired into the `needs` of both `quick-test-gate` and `full-test-gate`, so a Windows storage regression blocks both PR merges and the merge queue. Since the selected tests are deterministic `user`-fixture tests (no Selenium), there is no flakiness risk in the gate. - **Verified red→green on real Windows** (from #6159): with the fix present, the file-race test passes; with `unlink_with_retry` reverted to a plain `unlink()`, it fails with `PermissionError: [WinError 32]`. On Linux it is green either way — which is exactly why this leg exists.
Why the browser tests are excluded 25 of the storage tests use the Selenium `screen` fixture and are intermittently flaky on `windows-2022` for reasons unrelated to storage: `Timed out receiving message from renderer` in the browser, and a `ConnectionResetError: [WinError 10054]` from the Windows Proactor event loop during teardown that `filterwarnings = error` elevates to a failure. An earlier draft of this PR ran the full file with `pytest-rerunfailures --reruns 2` as a safety net; excluding the browser tests via the `screen` marker removes the flakiness at the root instead, and loses nothing relevant — the Windows-only failure mode lives entirely in the file layer, which the browser-independent tests cover.

## Summary

Fixes #1512, following @piyushumate's direction there: the inference
added in #1451 stays the default, and GPT-OSS passes its rotary width
explicitly.

Since #1451, `rope_forward` infers `rotary_dim = min(cos.shape[-1],
head_dim)`. GPT-OSS's rotary embedding returns cos/sin of width
`head_dim / 2` (`emb = freqs`, not `cat(freqs, freqs)`) while its
`apply_rotary_pos_emb` rotates the whole head, so the patched GPT-OSS
was treated as partial RoPE over the first half of each head, with no
error.

Changes:

- `rope_forward` / `rope_backward`, `LigerRopeFunction`, `liger_rope`
and `liger_rotary_pos_emb` take an optional `rotary_dim`. `None` keeps
today's inference. An explicit value must be even, at most `head_dim`,
and cos/sin must have at least `rotary_dim / 2` entries, otherwise a
`ValueError` is raised.
- New `liger_rotary_pos_emb_gpt_oss`, which calls
`liger_rotary_pos_emb(..., rotary_dim=head_dim)`.
`apply_liger_kernel_to_gpt_oss` now patches that in.
- Backends: `nvidia-triton` forwards `rotary_dim`. `nvidia-cutedsl`
already routes cos/sin narrower than `head_dim` to Triton and now also
does so for an explicit partial `rotary_dim`. `ascend-triton` accepts
`rotary_dim` only when it equals `head_dim`, since it does not implement
partial RoPE.

## Details

The Triton kernel itself is unchanged. With `rotary_dim = head_dim` it
reads the first `head_dim / 2` entries of cos/sin, which is what 0.8.4
did and what GPT-OSS's layout provides.

`LigerRopeFunction.backward` returns one more `None` for the new input.

Fix short-circuit skipping AssetManager cleanup on engage retraction (#7914)

Fixes a short-circuiting `||` in
`RetractEngageWorkflowOperationHandler.start()` that let a successful
`removeFromEngage()` call skip `removeFromArchive()` entirely, so the
`engage-player` publication was never stripped from the media package
during `retract-for-deletion`. `RetractionListener` then refused to
complete the deletion, leaving the event gone from search but
permanently stuck in the Asset Manager.

To reproduce: publish an event to Engage, then delete it via the
External API (`DELETE /api/events/{id}`). The retraction workflow
completes, but the event stays behind indefinitely with its
`engage-player` publication still attached.

The fix evaluates both cleanup calls unconditionally instead of
short-circuiting, matching the original intent of a468a0bfe9 ("Always
remove publication from AM on retraction").

### How to test this patch

1. Ingest and process an event so it publishes to Engage.
2. Confirm `processing_state` is `SUCCEEDED` via `GET /api/events/{id}`.
3. `DELETE /api/events/{id}` and wait for the `retract-for-deletion`
workflow to finish.
4. `GET /api/events/{id}` should now return `404`. Before this fix, it
kept returning `200` with `publication_status: ["engage-player"]`.

Unit tests are included: `RetractEngageWorkflowOperationHandlerTest`
covers the successful-retraction case (the regression), the
already-gone-from-search case, and the nothing-to-retract `SKIP` case.

[CUDA] Route training-only cuDNN calls through the runtime loader (#33744)

### Description

#29252 made cuDNN optional at runtime: the CUDA provider no longer links
cuDNN and forwards every cuDNN call through `cudnn_stub.cc` to the
dynamically loaded library. The stub covers the inference path but not
these eight functions, which only the training kernels in
`orttraining/orttraining/training_ops/cuda/nn/` call (`conv_grad.cc`,
`conv_transpose_grad.cc`, `conv_shared.cc`, `batch_norm_grad.cc`):

- `cudnnBatchNormalizationBackward`
- `cudnnConvolutionBackwardBias`
- `cudnnConvolutionBackwardFilter`
- `cudnnFindConvolutionBackwardFilterAlgorithmEx`
- `cudnnGetConvolutionBackwardDataAlgorithm_v7`
- `cudnnGetConvolutionBackwardDataWorkspaceSize`
- `cudnnGetConvolutionBackwardFilterAlgorithm_v7`
- `cudnnGetConvolutionBackwardFilterWorkspaceSize`

This PR adds a forwarding stub for each one, using the same
`ORT_CUDNN_FORWARD_STATUS` pattern as the rest of the file. The
signatures match the cuDNN 9 headers (`cudnn_cnn.h`, `cudnn_ops.h`).

### Motivation and Context

Fixes #33638. With `onnxruntime_ENABLE_TRAINING=ON` these eight are left
as undefined references in `libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so`, which has
no `DT_NEEDED` on `libcudnn.so.9`. The provider fails to load
(`undefined symbol: cudnnGetConvolutionBackwardDataAlgorithm_v7`) and
sessions silently fall back to CPU, inference included. This breaks Arch
Linux's `onnxruntime-cuda` package, which builds with training on.

### Testing

On WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 13.3 (V13.3.73), cuDNN 9.20.0.48, RTX 5070 Ti
Laptop (sm_120): `build.py --use_cuda --enable_training
--build_shared_lib --targets onnxruntime_providers_cuda` with
`CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120`, from this branch.

```
$ nm -D --undefined-only libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so | grep -c cudnn
0
$ readelf -d libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so | grep NEEDED

 0x0000000000000001 (NEEDED)             Shared library: [libcublas.so.13]
 0x0000000000000001 (NEEDED)             Shared library: [libcudart.so.13]
 0x0000000000000001 (NEEDED)             Shared library: [libcuda.so.1]
 0x0000000000000001 (NEEDED)             Shared library: [libstdc++.so.6]
 0x0000000000000001 (NEEDED)             Shared library: [libm.so.6]
 0x0000000000000001 (NEEDED)             Shared library: [libgcc_s.so.1]
 0x0000000000000001 (NEEDED)             Shared library: [libc.so.6]
 0x0000000000000001 (NEEDED)             Shared library: [ld-linux-x86-64.so.2]
$ nm --defined-only libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so | grep -wE 'cudnnCreate|cudnnBatchNormalizationBackward|cudnnGetConvolutionBackwardFilterWorkspaceSize'
0000000000375940 t cudnnCreate
0000000000376cb0 t cudnnBatchNormalizationBackward

Fix ui.select(with_input) dropping its html_id (breaks tooltips) (#6116)

*Posted by Claude Code on @evnchn's behalf.*

### Motivation

Fixes #6114.

`ui.select(with_input=True)` doesn't show a tooltip added via
`.tooltip()`. The browser console shows `Anchor: target "#cN" not
found`, and `ui.query(f'#{select.html_id}')` can't target the element
either.

**Root cause:** `.tooltip()` anchors its `QTooltip` with
`target="#{html_id}"`, relying on the element's `id` landing on a DOM
node. In `use-input` mode, Quasar's `QSelect` assigns the inner
`<input>` a generated id (its `targetUid`, e.g. `f_<uuid>`), which
displaces NiceGUI's fall-through `id`. As a result no DOM element
carries `cN`, so the tooltip anchor (and `ui.query('#...')`) resolve to
nothing.

Verified against the rendered DOM: a plain `ui.select` keeps its id on
the persistent `q-field__native` div, and `ui.input` / `ui.number` /
`ui.textarea` are unaffected — **only `with_input` selects** drop the
id.

### Implementation

Set Quasar's `for` prop to the element's `html_id` in the `with_input`
branch. `for` is Quasar's documented way to set the inner control's id,
so the input's id becomes `html_id` again and the anchor target exists:

```python
self._props['for'] = self.html_id
```

fix(query): keep pacman.conf repo order for exact name matches (#2987)

Motivation
With separatesources enabled (the default), a package with the exact
searched name that exists in several sync repos can be listed in the
wrong order. For example, if [cachyos-extra-v3] comes before [extra] in
pacman.conf, extra/chromium can still show up as the top pick instead of
cachyos-extra-v3/chromium. pacman prefers the repo listed first.

separateSourceScore returned a flat 50 for every exact match, whatever
its source. As a result, all exact matches got the same metric
(50 + 1.0). The unstable slices.SortFunc then left their relative order
unspecified, so the ordering added for non-exact results did not apply
to exact ones.

Approach
Move the repo-order scoring into a repoOrderScore helper (same logic and
cache as before). For exact matches, add repoOrderScore/separateSourceMax
to the 50: a bonus between 0 and 1. Exact matches still outrank every
non-exact result (which scores at most 45 + a metric below 1). Among
exact matches, repos earlier in pacman.conf now come first. Exact AUR
matches keep 50, so an exact sync-repo match now ranks strictly above an
exact AUR match instead of tying with it. Scoring for non-exact results
is unchanged, and nothing changes when separatesources is disabled.

## Problem

When a page with `ssr = false` is loaded directly, `afterNavigate` gets
an `enter` navigation with `from: { route: { id: null }, url: null, … }`
instead of `null`, so `navigation.from?.url.pathname` throws.
`create_navigation()` builds `from` from `current`, which is still empty
before the first page loads. The hydrating start path already passes
`from: null`.

`create_navigation()` sets `from` to `null` for `enter` navigations, so
both start paths match.

A new test in the `SPA mode / no SSR` group expects `from: null` on a
client-rendered page. It fails without the change. Navigation, snapshot
and SPA tests in `basics` pass in dev, build, server-side route
resolution and async mode, as do unit tests, lint and `pnpm check`. With
a packed build of this branch, the repro from the issue shows `from:
null`.
