Add response body flow control (#2318)

## Summary

- Add a thread-safe `ResponseBodyControl` callback after final response
headers.
- Support suspending, resuming, and cancelling HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
response bodies without coupling AHC to a streaming API.
- Pause the network read timeout while reads are intentionally suspended
while leaving the request timeout active.
- Keep suspended HTTP/2 streams independent and cover transport
backpressure, cancellation, timeouts, and connection reuse.

## Motivation

AHC 3 removed `StreamedAsyncHandler` and its Reactive Streams
integration in pull request
[#1843](https://github.com/AsyncHttpClient/async-http-client/pull/1843).
That removal avoids coupling AHC to a particular streaming library, but
`AsyncHandler` by itself has no way to stop transport reads while a
downstream consumer has no demand.

[Play WS](https://github.com/playframework/play-ws) is the driving
consumer for this change. Play WS needs transport backpressure to
preserve its existing Pekko Streams and Reactive Streams response APIs
while upgrading to AHC 3. A working adapter on a currently local Play WS
development branch turns this control into a single-subscriber Reactive
Streams publisher and has been tested against this AHC branch.

This pull request adds only the transport primitive. Streaming-library
policy and dependencies remain in Play WS, so AHC does not regain a
dependency on Reactive Streams or JDK Flow.

## Semantics

- `AsyncHandler.onResponseBodyStart` runs after final headers and before
body parts, including for a response with no body.
- Calls to the supplied control are thread-safe, idempotent, and ignored
after response completion.
- `suspend()` stops requesting new transport data, although body parts
already read may still be delivered.
- `resume()` permits transport reads again.
- Returning `State.ABORT` is the synchronous callback-time way to stop
processing. A handler can retain the control and call `cancel()` when an
asynchronous decision is made after the callback returns.
- Cancelling an HTTP/1.1 body closes its connection when bytes may
remain unread; cancellation after terminal content has been received can
reuse a keep-alive connection. Cancelling an HTTP/2 body closes only its
stream.
- Fully consumed responses retain the existing HTTP/1.1 pooling and
HTTP/2 parent-connection reuse behavior.
- Suspension pauses only the network read timeout. The request timeout
remains active; if the request timeout is disabled, an application that
never resumes or cancels can retain the exchange and its transport
resources indefinitely.

## HTTP/2 flow control

Connections with no actively suspended response retain Netty's normal
connection-level receive-window accounting. The default 65,535-byte
connection window therefore continues to cap unconsumed flow-controlled
DATA across all streams for users that never call `suspend()`.

When the first response on a connection is suspended, AHC returns
connection-level credit that has already accumulated and continues
returning that shared credit as DATA arrives. This prevents the
suspended stream from exhausting the connection window and starving
sibling streams. Per-stream credit remains consumption-driven at all
times, so each suspended stream is still bounded by its own receive
window. Multiple simultaneous suspensions are counted, and normal
connection accounting resumes after the last one ends. Credit already
returned and data already queued cannot be revoked, and the controller
tracks credit returned early so later application consumption does not
return it twice.

During an active suspension, aggregate buffering can still scale with
the number of concurrent streams; the relevant controls are
`http2InitialWindowSize`, `http2MaxConcurrentStreams`, and the
connection limits. The defaults do not impose a hard client-side
aggregate bound during that interval: the initial per-stream window is
16 MiB and `http2MaxConcurrentStreams = -1` leaves concurrency
server-controlled. A rough upper-bound estimate is connection count
times effective concurrent streams times the initial window, excluding
network and decoder overhead. Applications requiring a finite policy
must configure these values together. A hard aggregate byte budget is a
separate design and is outside this pull request.

Netty's connection auto-refill state is private and fixed when
`DefaultHttp2LocalFlowController` is constructed, so it cannot be
enabled only for the lifetime of a suspension through composition or
subclassing. The package-private
`SuspensionAwareHttp2LocalFlowController` therefore adapts
`DefaultHttp2LocalFlowController` from Netty 4.2.17.Final, preserving
its normal behavior while making connection refill suspension-scoped.

This adaptation has a maintenance cost: AHC owns the copied flow-control
logic and every Netty upgrade must compare it with the corresponding
upstream implementation for correctness and security fixes. The exact
source version and that obligation are recorded in the class Javadoc. An
upstream Netty API that permits connection auto-refill to be changed at
runtime would provide the exit path and allow AHC to remove the
adaptation; no such API exists in Netty 4.2.17.Final.

The auto-refill mode requires a custom `Http2Connection`. Netty's
builder treats `server()` and `connection()` as mutually exclusive, so
`ClientHttp2FrameCodecBuilder` supplies the connection through the
protected builder API and overrides `isServer()` to retain client mode.

The explicit `gracefulShutdownTimeoutMillis(0)` is not a new shutdown
policy. `Http2FrameCodecBuilder.forClient()` selects zero through its
package-private client constructor; the subclass must use the protected
no-argument constructor, so it sets zero explicitly to preserve the
existing client-factory behavior.

## Scope and commit structure

The API/lifecycle work and the HTTP/2 independence work are kept as
separate logical commits, but they belong in one pull request. Without
the HTTP/2 work, a suspended response can consume the shared connection
window and block unrelated sibling streams, so the public control would
not have correct multiplexed behavior. Follow-up review fixes are also
split into focused commits covering exchange ownership, terminal
cleanup, terminal HTTP/1.1 cancellation, bodyless responses, interim
responses, indefinite-suspension diagnostics, and suspension-scoped
HTTP/2 refill.

## History checked

- Issue
[#544](https://github.com/AsyncHttpClient/async-http-client/issues/544)
originally identified the lack of `AsyncHandler` backpressure, and pull
request
[#963](https://github.com/AsyncHttpClient/async-http-client/pull/963)
addressed it by adding Reactive Streams support.
- Issues
[#1233](https://github.com/AsyncHttpClient/async-http-client/issues/1233)
and
[#1721](https://github.com/AsyncHttpClient/async-http-client/issues/1721)
document the interaction between downstream demand and read timeouts in
the former streamed handler.
- Pull request
[#1843](https://github.com/AsyncHttpClient/async-http-client/pull/1843)
removed `StreamedAsyncHandler` for AHC 3.
- Discussion
[#1925](https://github.com/AsyncHttpClient/async-http-client/discussions/1925)
asks how to migrate streamed consumers to AHC 3; the maintainer response
declines restoring Reactive Streams because other libraries provide that
policy and maintaining it adds overhead.
- Focused GitHub issue, pull-request, discussion, and local history
searches found no existing AHC 3 proposal for a
streaming-library-neutral suspend/resume/cancel response-body control.

## Compatibility

- `AsyncHandler.onResponseBodyStart` is a new Java `default` method, so
existing handler implementations remain source- and binary-compatible
and retain their previous behavior unless they override it.
- `ResponseBodyControl` is a new public interface.
- `NettyResponseBodyControl` is public only to support AHC's
cross-package transport integration and is marked `@ApiStatus.Internal`;
consumers should depend on `ResponseBodyControl` instead.
- HTTP/1.1 informational responses from 102 through 199 are now treated

`onHeadersReceived`; this matches the existing HTTP/2 behavior and
prevents a 103 Early Hints response from completing the exchange before
the final response. Existing 100 Continue handling and 101 protocol
switching are preserved.
- Cancelling HTTP/1.1 processing from a terminal trailer or body
callback now reuses a keep-alive connection because `LastHttpContent`
has already been received; it previously closed that fully read
connection.

refactor: modernize URL patterns with Django path() (#12984)

Replaces legacy `re_path()` with `path()` typed converters where regex
is unnecessary across `builds/urls.py`, `projects/urls/private.py`,
`projects/urls/public.py`, and `gold/urls.py`.

## URL patterns (`re_path` → `path`)

Converted `[-\w]+`, `\d+`, and `[^/]+` patterns to typed path
converters.

**Before:**
```python
re_path(r"^(?P<project_slug>[-\w]+)/version/(?P<version_slug>[^/]+)/edit/$", ...)
re_path(r"^(?P<project_slug>[-\w]+)/redirects/(?P<redirect_pk>\d+)/insert/(?P<position>\d+)/$", ...)
```

**After:**
```python
path("<slug:project_slug>/version/<str:version_slug>/edit/", ...)
path("<slug:project_slug>/redirects/<int:redirect_pk>/insert/<int:position>/", ...)
```

One exception: the automation rule `move` URL keeps `re_path` because
`steps` allows negative integers (`-?\d+`) which `<int:>` does not
support.

`<str:version_slug>` is used instead of `<slug:version_slug>` because
`VERSION_SLUG_REGEX` allows dots (e.g. `1.0`, `3.2.1`), which Django's
`<slug:>` converter (`[-a-zA-Z0-9_]+`) does not match.

Also updated `test_privacy_urls.py`'s `_test_url()` helper — it
extracted named parameters via `re.compile(regex).groupindex`, which
breaks for `path()` route strings. Now handles both syntaxes.

Merged PR 2335611: Allow explicit RC installs with release-provided checksums

The installer always uses the stable repository, even when downloaded from RC1. Add an explicit `--version vX.Y-RCN` while preserving the stable default.

RC packages are selected from that release's `SHA256SUMS` by OS, architecture and PostgreSQL major, and each is verified over HTTPS before installation. No version, filename or digest is hardcoded, so a new RC needs no installer change and rebuilt packages work once their published checksums are updated. Missing, ambiguous or mismatched packages stop installation without falling back to stable. RCs require a clean host: installed, removed-but-not-purged or half-installed DocumentDB packages, leftover configuration or data, and a configured stable repository are refused. RC installs cannot be adopted by a later stable installer run.

No workflow changes or published release changes are included.

Security: tighten redirect URI matching to prevent prefix-confusion attacks (FireWatch c1bf88bd), Fixes AB#3665141 (#3136)

Fixes
[AB#3665141](https://identitydivision.visualstudio.com/fac9d424-53d2-45c0-91b5-ef6ba7a6bf26/_workitems/edit/3665141)
— redirect URI prefix-confusion hardening.

## Summary

Tighten redirect URI matching in
`AzureActiveDirectoryWebViewClient.isRedirectUrl` to use **structured
scheme + authority + path comparison** instead of `String#startsWith`,
eliminating a prefix-confusion attack vector. Gated by an ECS kill
switch.

## Why

`isRedirectUrl` used
`url.startsWith(mRedirectUrl.toLowerCase(Locale.US))`. Because
`startsWith` is a prefix match, a URL such as

```
msauth://com.outlook/HASH=.attacker.com/x?code=<AUTH_CODE>
```

passed the check for the registered redirect URI
`msauth://com.outlook/HASH=`, and the OAuth2 auth code was handed to
`processRedirectUrl()` on a URL controlled by an attacker. eSTS performs
**exact** redirect URI validation server-side, but the client check
should be exact too (defense-in-depth, MSRC Ceiling Rule 3).

## What changes

**`isRedirectUrl()`** — replaced the prefix match with `Uri.parse`-based
comparison requiring scheme + authority (host[:port]) + path to all
match (case-insensitive). Query and fragment are ignored (they carry
`code`/`state` on legit redirects). A single trailing slash on the path
is normalized, so a registered `/auth` still matches an incoming
`/auth/`. Any other path difference is rejected. Unparseable URLs fail
closed (`false`).

**Opaque redirect URIs (e.g. the broker OOB redirect
`urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob`)** — opaque URIs have null authority/path,
so a naive scheme+authority+path comparison would degenerate to
scheme-only and accept any same-scheme `urn:*`. These are now compared
by scheme-specific part (minus any appended `?query`/`#fragment`), and a
spoofed URI must be opaque on both sides. Parse-failure logging records
the exception **type only** (never the throwable message, which could
embed the URL and thus the auth code).

**ECS kill switch** — `ENABLE_STRICT_REDIRECT_URI_MATCHING` CommonFlight
(default **on**). When disabled via ECS, `isRedirectUrl` reverts to the
historical `String#startsWith` behavior, allowing a config-only rollback
without a code change.

## ⚠️ Known limitation — msauth:// install path (tracked as follow-up)

For **msauth:// redirect URIs (the broker case)**, this fix alone is
**not** sufficient. After `isRedirectUrl` correctly rejects a spoofed
`msauth://…` URL, the very next branch in `handleUrl` —
`isInstallRequestUrl` (`BROWSER_EXT_INSTALL_PREFIX = "msauth://"`) —
matches **any** `msauth://` URL, and `processInstallRequest` also calls
`RawAuthorizationResult.fromRedirectUri(url)`, delivering the code to
the completion callback. So for msauth the prefix-confusion outcome is
unchanged at the callback.

The fix **is** effective for non-msauth (e.g. `https://`, custom-scheme)
redirect URIs, which is why the new tests use an `https://` redirect URI
to isolate and prove the `isRedirectUrl` behavior.

**Behavior delta for msauth (no regression):** only the *routing* of a
spoofed/suffixed `msauth://` URL changes — it now falls through from
`isRedirectUrl` to `isInstallRequestUrl` and is handled by
`processInstallRequest` instead of `processRedirectUrl`. The auth-code
outcome at the callback is identical (both deliver the same `COMPLETED`
result), so **no legitimate redirect or install request changes
behavior**. The only observable difference is for attack/malformed
traffic: it is now logged and counted as a broker-install step
(`STEP_BROKER_INSTALL_PROMPTED`) rather than a redirect — cosmetic, and
fully reverted by the `ENABLE_STRICT_REDIRECT_URI_MATCHING` kill switch.

**Plan:** closing the msauth path (tightening `isInstallRequestUrl` /
`processInstallRequest` so a generic `msauth://…?code=…` without
`app_link`/`wpj` is not treated as an install request) will be handled
as a **separate follow-up PR**, to keep this defense-in-depth change
focused and independently shippable.

## Tests

Assert the real security property via the completion callback (not just
the `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` return value), using `https://` and
opaque `urn:` redirect URIs:

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `testStrictMatching_acceptsLegitimateHttpsRedirect` | Legit redirect
-> code delivered once |
| `testStrictMatching_acceptsTrailingSlashPathDifference` | `/auth`
registered, `/auth/` incoming -> still delivered |
| `testStrictMatching_acceptsLegitimateOpaqueOobRedirect` | Legit
`urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob?code=…` -> code delivered (COMPLETED) |
| `testStrictMatching_rejectsSpoofedOpaqueOobRedirect` |
`urn:…:oobstolen?code=…` -> never delivered as COMPLETED |
| `testStrictMatching_rejectsSpoofedRedirectWithSuffixHost` |
`…/auth.attacker.com/x?code=…` -> callback never invoked |
| `testStrictMatching_rejectsSpoofedRedirectWithPathSuffix` |
`…/authstolen?code=…` -> callback never invoked |
| `testKillSwitch_disablesStrictMatching_revertsToPrefixMatch` | Flag
off -> prefix match restored, spoof delivered again |
| `testUrlOverrideHandlesRedirectUriString` / `…WithFragment` | msauth
legit redirect (query / fragment) still handled |

Merged PR 2360765: Add gateway backend connection metrics, operation duration buckets, and documentdb-local metrics enablement

### Does this PR have any customer impact?

Yes. With OpenTelemetry metrics enabled, the standalone gateway publishes backend connection pool metrics and a backend connection creation counter, and records `docdb.gateway.operation.duration` with explicit bucket boundaries. documentdb-local `--enable-telemetry true` now enables gateway OTLP metrics. With metrics disabled, behavior is unchanged.

### Type

Feature.

### Does it involve schema level changes?

No.

### Are you introducing any new config?

No. documentdb-local `--enable-telemetry true` (or `ENABLE_TELEMETRY=true`) also sets `OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED=true` unless it is already set.

### ChangeLog

Publish gateway backend connection metrics and let documentdb-local telemetry enable gateway OTLP metrics.

**Breaking change:** the shipped `SetupConfiguration.json` no longer sets `TelemetryOptions.Metrics` or `TelemetryOptions.Tracing`, so `OTEL_*` environment variables now configure gateway telemetry. To keep telemetry off regardless of the environment, set `TelemetryOptions.Metrics.Enabled` and `TelemetryOptions.Tracing.Enabled` to `false`.

### Description

- Pool gauges `docdb.backend.connection_pool.usage` (by `db.client.connection.state`: `used`, `idle`), `docdb.backend.connection_pool.limit`, and `docdb.backend.connection_pool.wait.active`, sampled every five seconds while request metrics are enabled, plus the `docdb.backend.connection_pool.timeout.count` counter. `docdb.backend.connection_pool.role` carries a bounded pool role: `system_requests`, `pre_auth_requests`, or `data`. Every pool that runs client data requests reports as `data`.
- `docdb.backend.connection.create.count` counts creation attempts; failures carry `error.type` of `auth`, `connection_limit`, `network`, or `other`.
- `docdb.gateway.operation.duration` uses explicit boundaries from 0.005 to 300 seconds; other histograms keep the SDK defaults.
- The sample `SetupConfiguration.json` no longer pins metrics or tracing settings, so `OTEL_*` variables apply. CONTRIBUTING describes enablement.
- documentdb-local help describes OTLP export and its endpoint variable.
- Cardinality: at most 15 pool series and 15 creation series per process, excluding resource attributes.

fix(storage): sign OCI images as cosign/sign/v1 (#2096)

In sigstore-bundle mode the image signature was a simplesigning
payload signed over its raw bytes, wrapped in a DSSE envelope and
logged to Rekor as a hashedrekord entry. A DSSE bundle needs an
in-toto payload, a signature over the DSSE PAE and a dsse Rekor
entry, so no verifier accepted it. `cosign verify` hid this whenever
the SLSA attestation bundle was also present, because it succeeds if
any bundle verifies.

The encoding mode now decides the image-signature payload. dsse is
unchanged. sigstore-bundle uses a new internal cosign-sign/v1
payload: an in-toto Statement with the image as subject, predicateType
https://sigstore.dev/cosign/sign/v1 and an empty predicate, as
`cosign sign` v3 produces. It goes through the existing wrapped DSSE
signer, a dsse Rekor entry and AttestationStorer, so no new bundle
writer is needed. The broken SimpleStorer bundle path is removed.

sigstore-bundle now requires artifacts.oci.storage to be "oci" only;
the config is rejected at load time otherwise, because the other
backends expect a simplesigning payload for OCI images.

Tests verify the stored bundle with sigstore-go and add e2e cases that
run cosign v3 against the registry. The e2e registry is addressed by
its ClusterIP so go-containerregistry uses plain HTTP for the referrer
manifest write.

fix(autolock): assign timer entry after write to close start/cancel race

start() assigned the in-memory `_entry` before the awaited
`store.write(...)`. A cancel() that interleaved while start() was
suspended at that write cleared `_entry`, so start() resumed into
`_schedule_remaining()` and tripped `assert self._entry is not None`
(AssertionError). This is the start()-side mirror of the cancel() race
fixed in #703.

Assign `_entry` from a local after the write returns, keeping start()'s
post-write tail synchronous and atomic. This also subsumes the
persistence half of the race: with the tail synchronous, no two-actor
start/cancel interleaving can leave the timer ACTIVE in memory while the
store entry is absent (or vice versa) -- both lock orderings end in a
consistent (memory, disk) pair.

Closes #748

## Changes

- **IPC:** Append the native ContentProvider operation at ordinal 35
with five caller fields, dedicated success/unknown-outcome codes and no
AccountManager fallback.
- **Protocol:** Require host `6.0`, following the existing host-version
convention, plus a fresh, exactly Boolean-true HELLO handler capability.
Preserve every existing host/MSAL minimum and Broker selection behavior.
- **Assertion format:** Document the implemented compact ES256 JWT,
separate Broker WPJ wrapping and a synthetic example; this is not a raw
FIDO assertion envelope.
- **HTTP:** Add per-instance redirect, fixed-length streaming, cache,
response-byte-limit, strict UTF-8 and IO-redaction controls. Preserve
the seven-argument constructor, legacy defaults and default-client
bounded retries; native consumers explicitly use `NoRetryPolicy`.
- **Privacy and cleanup:** Redact IO details before exception-time
telemetry and preserve primary failures during stream cleanup.
- **Regression sources:** Cover compatibility, transport boundaries,
setup failures and cancellation in native/legacy modes, no replay,
callback cleanup and normal telemetry privacy.

## Validation and scope

Static checks passed. Local tests, compilation, lint and manual E2E
remain deferred by request; repository CI runs independently and must be
checked for this head.

This is a prerequisite contract, not an implemented Broker recovery
handler, lifecycle-safe storage commit or MAM-success guarantee. No
artifact release is claimed. Alignment of this implementation with the
linked FIDO design/service profile remains unresolved.

fix(tvd): return zero loss for an all-ignored batch (#1565)

Fixes #1564

## Summary

`LigerTVDLoss` divided by `n_non_ignore` before launching the kernel.
When every `shift_labels` entry is `ignore_index`, `n_non_ignore == 0`,
so `batchmean` and `mean` raised `ZeroDivisionError`. This adds a
`n_non_ignore == 0 -> scale = 0.0` guard, matching the existing fused
linear KL loss. The kernel then writes zero loss and zero gradients;
`sum` and `none` were already correct and are unchanged.

## Before / after (RTX A5000, torch 2.8.0+cu128, triton 3.4.0)

Before:

```
batchmean ERR ZeroDivisionError float division by zero
mean     ERR ZeroDivisionError float division by zero
sum      -> tensor(0.)
none     -> all-zero tensor
```

After: all four reductions return zero loss / zero gradients, and match
the existing `TorchTVDLoss` reference.

## Verification

```bash
python -m pytest test/transformers/test_tvd.py -q --disable-warnings --no-header -k "not torch_compile"
# 196 passed, 40 skipped, 4 deselected

ruff check src/liger_kernel/ops/tvd.py test/transformers/test_tvd.py
ruff format --check --diff src/liger_kernel/ops/tvd.py test/transformers/test_tvd.py
# All checks passed! / 2 files already formatted
```

The new `test_correctness_all_ignored` covers `batchmean`, `sum`,
`mean`, and `none` with all labels set to `ignore_index`. On `main`, the
`batchmean` and `mean` cases fail with the `ZeroDivisionError` above.

The 4 deselected tests are the existing
`test_torch_compile_matches_eager` cases; they fail identically on
unmodified `main` in this environment (torch 2.8.0 / triton 3.4.0),
unrelated to this change.

[AI] MacOS: activate app when re-showing an already shown form

Clicking "Show OpenTabletDriver" in the tray icon did not bring the
window to the front when the form was already shown.

Eto's Form.Show() only calls the handler's Show() the first time the
form is shown (when !Loaded); every later call just sets Visible = true,
so the existing FormHandler.Show() override with
ActivateIgnoringOtherApps() never ran on the re-show path.

Bringing the window forward in BringToFront() was not an option because
it cannot be overridden: Window.BringToFront() is a plain non-virtual
method that forwards to the handler, and the Mac handler's BringToFront()
is non-virtual as well (it only calls NSWindow.orderFront, which
reorders windows within our own app and does not activate the app, so
it would not foreground the window anyway). Visible, on the other hand,
is virtual on the handler and is the single choke point that every
re-show path goes through: the tray menu item, Form.Show() on an
already loaded form, and the hide-to-tray restore in MainForm.

Upstream, picoe/Eto#2964 ("Mac: Bring focused windows to the
foreground") is still open and the maintainer would prefer an
Application.Instance.Activate() API over activating on every window
focus, so it will likely take some time to land. This keeps the
workaround local until then.

References:
- https://github.com/picoe/Eto/blob/2.11.0/src/Eto/Forms/Window.cs
  "public void BringToFront() => Handler.BringToFront();" is not virtual,
  so no subclass or handler override can inject app activation there.
- https://github.com/picoe/Eto/blob/2.11.0/src/Eto/Forms/Form.cs
  Form.Show(): "var loaded = Loaded; if (!loaded) { ... Handler.Show(); }
  else { base.Visible = true; }" — re-showing an already loaded form
  bypasses the handler's Show() entirely and goes through Visible.
- https://github.com/picoe/Eto/blob/2.11.0/src/Eto.Mac/Forms/MacWindow.cs
  Mac handler BringToFront() only does "Control.OrderFront(Control)",
  which cannot activate a background application.
- https://github.com/picoe/Eto/pull/2964
  Open upstream fix for foregrounding windows on Mac; still under
  discussion (maintainer prefers an Application.Instance.Activate()
  API), so it will probably take some time to land.

Open the repository with gitoxide too

A transaction now carries the gitoxide view of its repository beside
the libgit2 one, ready for the object and ref reads to move over.

It is held in thread-safe form and handed out per call as a
`gix::Repository`: a transaction crosses threads, which josh-graphql
requires, while the thread-local handle holds `Rc` snapshots of
packed-refs and shallow state and cannot. That also means the workspace
builds gix with `parallel`, without which even the thread-safe handle
is `Rc`-based.

The opened repositories are shared for the whole process, keyed by
repository path in the shape of josh-memodb's store registry, rather
than once per context: the proxy builds a context per request, and a
per-request open costs twice over -- opening reads configuration and
resolves alternates, and the pack indices a store discovers start
cold each time. Measured against a mirror-shaped repository of 200
small packs, open-and-drop cost 3.9ms per fresh context against
0.09ms shared, and twenty packed blob reads cost 13.3ms through a
cold store against 0.12ms warm. Sharing across transactions rests on
the same properties as sharing within one: a store that misses an
object rescans its objects directory once all its known indices come
up empty, so a pack another transaction has just flushed is still
found, and ref reads see loose and packed files as they are.

A-1474: Remove --organization, --pipeline, --branch flags from cache subcommand

These flags on `cache save`/`restore` were client-controllable (defaulting
to BUILDKITE_* env vars) and sent verbatim on save, making scope labels
forgeable. Per the Cache Policy Design decision, save scope must equal the
verified agent identity, resolved server-side from the job/OIDC token.

Remove the flags, their plumbing through cache.Config and the client, and
the branch/pipeline/owner fields on CacheEntryCreateReq. The server derives
these from the authenticated identity.
